cycles.method: An event is one MIDI sequencer tick: the note hook runs in its interrupt (0x400a1e0c, vector 0x60), once per note a track sends, priced at 16 core cycles an instruction (the ColdFire V4 envelope Direct Jump's record uses). Static: 10,904 instructions, an upper bound from akl.s for the dearest tick, all eight MIDI tracks sending four notes each with every track's step answer uncached: per track one 64-step scan (at most 64 x 10 instructions of loop and about 190 around it, 832 measured) and three cached notes (97 measured), plus about 60 for the base's take dispatch and claim per note over USB. Measured on the card build under ot_emu --mkii (octabam 8250be0), 24 Oct 2026: PC watches on akl_note_entry and its two exits on a 64-step pattern whose only lock sits just after the notes (three tracks arpeggiating, every new step a full scan): at most 832 instructions a note, 70-97 cached, 1,856 in the dearest tick (5 notes). Budget: the next tick, 8.33 ms at the top tempo of 300 BPM, 2,200,000 cycles at 264 MHz. Not chip timing.

load.method: Emulator, not hardware: ot_emu --mkii --dsp --frame (octabam 8250be0, upstream:tools build), 24 Oct 2026. The original MAIN OS and the card build with ARP KEY LOCKS alone, the same 62 s from PLAY on the same project (a 64-step pattern, three MIDI tracks arpeggiating, a G PHR lock on track 1): one three-byte message every ms (note on, CC, note off on channels 1-8) and a clock byte every 10 ms (250 BPM), STOP and PLAY at 7, 22, 37 and 52 s, Part 2 and back at 30 and 31 s. Longest frame interrupt: the most instructions from the frame handler's entry 0x4000aad4 to its epilogue 0x4000d9a6 over 217,000 frames, 23,201 on both, priced in the port's time (3,990 instructions a sample, dsp.h g_cfIps). Idle: 100 x (1 - executed instructions / (3,990 x samples)) between the first and last frame. The module's work runs in the sequencer tick interrupt, which the frame interrupt preempts.

stress.droppedExplanation: Emulator, not hardware, the run above on the module image: 62,000 three-byte messages and 6,200 clock bytes; PC watches on the MIDI handlers (note on 0x4000e018, note off 0x4000db98, CC 0x4000e79c, clock 0x40005a48) counted every one, on both images, none missing. MIDI OUT: 206 note-ons and their note-offs on both images, 44 of them moved into the lock's key with the module; after the final STOP no note was left on, including the four STOPs that landed mid-note. Hangs: frames advanced to the end and the run ended on its own quit. Bypass: a pattern without locks plays stock's KEY (claims answer no; host test and the USB check).
